title: t01 FAA nationwide ground stop — narration (English)

chapters.title: A ground stop is a brake

items.title: It's Friday, November 13th, 2026
items.subtitle: It's Friday, November 13th, 2026, at 3:54 p.m. Eastern.

items.title: The FAA orders every
items.subtitle: The FAA orders every airport in the country: hold all departures until further notice.

items.title: The order cited "extraordinary
items.subtitle: The order cited "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety."

items.title: It lasted four hours
items.subtitle: It lasted four hours and twenty-one minutes.

items.title: Over 3,500 planes were in the air.
items.subtitle: Over 3,500 planes were in the air. All of them landed safely.

items.title: By that night
items.subtitle: By that night, over 4,400 flights were canceled, and over 10,000 delayed.

items.title: It was only the second nationwide
items.subtitle: It was only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11.

items.title: So why? There are two answers out there
items.subtitle: So why? There are two answers out there, and they sound like opposites.

items.title: The system's too old.
items.subtitle: The system's too old. Or an update knocked it out.

items.title: Our take? Both fall into the same trap.
items.subtitle: Our take? Both fall into the same trap.

items.title: Not the planes.
items.subtitle: Not the planes. Not the radar. A telecom network.

items.title: It links over 4,400
items.subtitle: It links over 4,400 air traffic facilities, including all 22 en route centers, which guide planes between airports.

items.title: Controllers' voices and radar
items.subtitle: Controllers' voices and radar data both run on it.

items.title: It's called FTI
items.subtitle: It's called FTI, the FAA's communications backbone, and a contractor, L3Harris, runs it.

items.title: The FAA's statement was short:
items.subtitle: The FAA's statement was short: multiple en route centers had communication issues, and technicians were investigating.

items.title: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy was blunter.
items.subtitle: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy was blunter. He called it an "incredibly old" system.

items.title: Old switches and routers, he said
items.subtitle: Old switches and routers, he said, couldn't handle the data.

items.title: And he stressed that none
items.subtitle: And he stressed that none of the new equipment went down.

items.title: Then he asked Congress for $50 billion.
items.subtitle: Then he asked Congress for $50 billion.

items.title: But CBS, citing unnamed sources
items.subtitle: But CBS, citing unnamed sources, said the network crashed after an update and a reboot.

items.title: That hasn't been confirmed.
items.subtitle: That hasn't been confirmed.

items.title: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne
items.subtitle: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin split the difference. He said new technology was overwhelming the old system.

items.title: As of November 14th
items.subtitle: As of November 14th, there's no official cause.

items.title: So we won't guess at this one.
items.subtitle: So we won't guess at this one. Let's look at the track record.

items.title: Here's what we noticed about
items.subtitle: Here's what we noticed about the worst nationwide failures in US air traffic control.

items.title: Each time, someone was in the middle
items.subtitle: Each time, someone was in the middle of changing something.

items.title: In November 2009
items.subtitle: In November 2009, it was the same network and the same company, back when it was called Harris.

items.title: They were moving data off the old
items.subtitle: They were moving data off the old network onto new fiber lines.

items.title: In Los Angeles
items.subtitle: In Los Angeles, a temporary router bridging the two networks was set up wrong.

items.title: Then the mistake was copied
items.subtitle: Then the mistake was copied onto the new router.

items.title: The damage should have stayed contained.
items.subtitle: The damage should have stayed contained. Instead, it hit 129 facilities.

items.title: The outage lasted five hours
items.subtitle: The outage lasted five hours and delayed 820 flights.

items.title: That's from the Transportation
items.subtitle: That's from the Transportation Department's inspector general.

items.title: August 2015. Washington's air traffic center
items.subtitle: August 2015. Washington's air traffic center had just upgraded its software.

items.title: A new feature filled up the memory.
items.subtitle: A new feature filled up the memory. Almost 500 flights were delayed, and nearly as many canceled.

items.title: January 2023. The system that sends
items.subtitle: January 2023. The system that sends notices to pilots crashed, and the whole country was grounded.

items.title: A contractor had deleted
items.subtitle: A contractor had deleted files during maintenance.

items.title: Congress's watchdog, the GAO
items.subtitle: Congress's watchdog, the GAO, says that system was over 30 years old.

items.title: Too old, or someone touched it?
items.subtitle: Too old, or someone touched it? Picking one is the trap. Here, it was both.

items.title: This time might be the same. Might.
items.subtitle: This time might be the same. Might.

items.title: Air traffic control never stops.
items.subtitle: Air traffic control never stops. You can't just reboot it like a laptop.

items.title: You have to upgrade it mid-flight
items.subtitle: You have to upgrade it mid-flight, a bit like swapping an engine in the air.

items.title: The new parts come in bit by bit
items.subtitle: The new parts come in bit by bit, while the old ones keep running.

items.title: The way we see it
items.subtitle: The way we see it, that overlap is when it's most fragile.

items.title: And the older it gets
items.subtitle: And the older it gets, the fewer people understand it, so every change gets riskier.

items.title: Riskier means nobody dares touch it.
items.subtitle: Riskier means nobody dares touch it. So it just keeps getting older.

items.title: We'd call that technical debt.
items.subtitle: We'd call that technical debt. Put it off, and the interest keeps piling up.

items.title: The evidence? In 2024
items.subtitle: The evidence? In 2024, the GAO checked 138 of the FAA's air traffic systems.

items.title: 51 couldn't be kept going.
items.subtitle: 51 couldn't be kept going. Another 54 might not be.

items.title: This September, the FAA's own administrator
items.subtitle: This September, the FAA's own administrator, Bryan Bedford, put it this way:

items.title: "We're pulling copper up
items.subtitle: "We're pulling copper up and putting fiber down, but it's the same data architecture that we've had for 50 years."

items.title: And the overlap keeps stretching.
items.subtitle: And the overlap keeps stretching.

items.title: The contract for the next
items.subtitle: The contract for the next network went to Verizon in 2023. This August, AT&T took over as lead.

items.title: Meanwhile, the old FTI network has to keep running.
items.subtitle: Meanwhile, the old FTI network has to keep running.

items.title: To be fair
items.subtitle: To be fair, it's not always a change that does it.

items.title: In Dallas in September 2025
items.subtitle: In Dallas in September 2025, two fiber lines were cut. The FAA says the contractor hadn't made sure the backup would work.

items.title: In Philadelphia this September
items.subtitle: In Philadelphia this September, the main line failed. The backup? Construction crews had already cut through it.

items.title: Back in 2004
items.subtitle: Back in 2004, Los Angeles had a different outage. The FAA says a required restart was skipped.

items.title: The system crashed.
items.subtitle: The system crashed. The backup crashed within a minute.

items.title: And FTI adds 150 to 200
items.subtitle: And FTI adds 150 to 200 new connections a month. Almost all of them go fine.

items.title: So we're only talking
items.subtitle: So we're only talking about the worst failures.

items.title: Look at how those backups failed.
items.subtitle: Look at how those backups failed.

items.title: A backup protects you when
items.subtitle: A backup protects you when things fail separately. Not when they fail together.

items.title: Same trench, same network, same contractor?
items.subtitle: Same trench, same network, same contractor? Then the backup only exists on paper.

items.title: As for why one fault went
items.subtitle: As for why one fault went nationwide this time, we'll have to wait for the investigation.

items.title: Critics would say we're just
items.subtitle: Critics would say we're just making excuses to stall.

items.title: Duffy himself said the new gear
items.subtitle: Duffy himself said the new gear held and the old gear broke.

items.title: They'd say: spend more and get it replaced faster.
items.subtitle: They'd say: spend more and get it replaced faster.

items.title: And saying upgrades are risky
items.subtitle: And saying upgrades are risky just scares people off.

items.title: We agree it has to be replaced. And fast.
items.subtitle: We agree it has to be replaced. And fast.

items.title: But we think the switchover
items.subtitle: But we think the switchover itself is the riskiest part, so plan for that.

items.title: The longer it drags on
items.subtitle: The longer it drags on, the longer that risky overlap lasts.

items.title: And money alone doesn't buy safety.
items.subtitle: And money alone doesn't buy safety.

items.title: This September, the GAO found no reliable estimate
items.subtitle: This September, the GAO found no reliable estimate of the new system's lifetime cost.

items.title: And the project runs on over 11,000
items.subtitle: And the project runs on over 11,000 separate schedules that don't fit together.

items.title: One last angle.
items.subtitle: One last angle. A nationwide ground stop looks like the system falling apart.

items.title: We'd argue it's the safety
items.subtitle: We'd argue it's the safety brake doing its job.

items.title: When the system can't be sure
items.subtitle: When the system can't be sure, it holds every departure. Costly, but safe.

items.title: And during the stop
items.subtitle: And during the stop, every plane in the air landed safely.

items.title: We think braking feels like failure
items.subtitle: We think braking feels like failure because you can see what it costs.

items.title: You can't see what it prevented.
items.subtitle: You can't see what it prevented.

items.title: If you can't live without a system
items.subtitle: If you can't live without a system, getting old is risky. Touching it is riskier.

items.title: So don't leave it alone.
items.subtitle: So don't leave it alone. Just be extra careful when you touch it.
